text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended easier but off the lows helped by late arbitrage buying against New York. Benchmark March lost $17 to close at $1,695 per tonne, while May gave up $8 to close at $1,686 per tonne. Conditions were dull and traders said the robusta market was probably heading for a pause, consolidating its recent gains after a new rally to $1,825 per tonne basis May, a peak not seen since last June. Arabica futures in New York rebounded after two consecutive sessions of losses to end sharply higher, boosted by speculative short-covering. March added 3.00 cents/lb to close at 205.00 cents/lb, while May added 4.10 cents/lb to close at 186.35 cents/lb. The outer months gained between 4.80 and 6.00 cents/lb. Traders will be keeping an eye on the Green Coffee Association of New York's monthly inventory data due after the close on March 17. Most market participants expect a modest rise in stocks. In January, supplies of green coffee stored in US warehouses rose by 15,000 60-kg bags to 1.342 mn bag

UNITED STATES - The CSCE reported certified coffee stocks grew for the seventh day in a row, reaching 44,983 bags as of March 13, up 2,650 bags on the previous day. There were an additional 27,946 bags pending grading, the exchange said.

UNITED STATES - Coffee roastings during the week ended March 8, totalled approximately 305,000 60-kg bags, down from 325,000 bags the previous week and compared with 310,000 bags in the corresponding week one year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage said. Cumulative roastings totalled 3.620 mn bags, versus 3.480 mn bags in the same year ago period, it was added.

COLOMBIA - Colombia raised its internal coffee price to a new high of 383,375 pesos per 125-kg load on March 14 in the sixth such increase since January 31, the National Coffee Growers' Federation said. The increases in producer prices are the result of higher world market prices.

SWEDEN - Sweden imported 160,415 bags of coffee in August 1996, 10 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 1.399 mn bags, 27 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 13 per cent to 1.648 mn bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/August 1996 were Guatemala (158,800 vs 123,200 bags), Brazil (272,200 vs 308,700 bags) and Colombia (298,300 vs 254,600 bags). The country exported 144,400 bags of coffee in January/August 1996, 11 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 8.6 per cent to 204,700 bags.
